briefing.summary: Strong risk-on momentum following a 6-day winning streak off the Aug 5 lows, fueled by blowout retail sales (+1.0% vs +0.3% expected), falling jobless claims, and CPI at 2.9%. Rally is extended approaching July highs—mean reversion and selective momentum plays appropriate in range-bound regime.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: July retail sales surged 1.0% MoM (consensus +0.3%), easing recession fears that drove the Aug 5 selloff. Weekly jobless claims fell to 227K (vs 235K est). CPI annual rate hit 2.9%, lowest since Mar 2021, cementing September rate cut expectations. Housing starts data due Aug 16 AM will show -6.8% to 1.2M annualized rate (weakest since May 2020). UMich preliminary consumer sentiment at 67.8, essentially flat. Macro picture is goldilocks: strong consumer, cooling inflation, labor market holding.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Walmart Q2 beat: EPS $0.67 vs $0.65, revenue $169.3B vs $168.6B, comp sales +4.2%, general merch positive first time in 11 quarters, raised FY guidance. Deere beat EPS ($6.29 vs $5.80) but revenue down 17% YoY to $13.15B. Applied Materials reported after close Aug 15: beat EPS $2.12 vs $2.01 and revenue $6.78B (+1.63% surprise). Target earnings upcoming Aug 21.

sections.title: Technicals
sections.content: S&P 500 at ~5,555 area on a 6-day win streak, recovered ~8% from Aug 5 intraday low. V-shaped recovery approaching July highs. RSI overbought on shorter timeframes. VIX collapsed from Aug 5 spike (38+) back to low-teens. Bitcoin stuck at $57-59K, below $60K resistance. Silver rallied 2.8% on Aug 15 to $28.36.

recommendations.thesis: AMAT beat on both top and bottom lines in a strong semi environment. The AI capex narrative gets another confirmation datapoint—if companies are spending more on semiconductor equipment, the entire AI supply chain thesis strengthens. With the broader market in risk-on mode, NVDA rallying, and positive macro data, AMAT should see post-earnings momentum. The stock closed at $208.58 before the after-hours print. Target $217 represents a 4.0% move vs 2.2% stop = 1.84:1 R:R, with the post-earnings gap-up dynamic front-loading the move.
recommendations.catalyst: Applied Materials reported Q3 earnings after close Aug 15: beat EPS by 5.5% ($2.12 vs $2.01) and revenue by 1.6% ($6.78B). Semiconductor capex cycle confirmed strong with AI-driven demand. Pre-market gap-up expected.

recommendations.thesis: NVDA is the AI bellwether recovering from the Aug 5 selloff. AMAT's beat on semi capex spending provides a direct positive read-through—if companies are spending more on semiconductor equipment, NVDA's datacenter GPU demand thesis strengthens further. With earnings Aug 28, institutional positioning typically begins 2 weeks out. The goldilocks macro (strong consumer + cooling inflation) supports growth/momentum names. Target 3.7% upside vs 2.2% downside = 1.7:1 R:R.
recommendations.catalyst: AMAT after-hours earnings beat confirms semiconductor capex cycle strength, providing positive read-through for NVDA. Pre-earnings run-up dynamic with NVDA reporting Aug 28. Risk-on macro environment (retail sales beat, falling claims) supports mega-cap growth leadership.

recommendations.thesis: BA has been one of the most beaten-down large-caps in 2024 due to quality/safety issues and trades well below historical range. The Aug 15 surge (+3.8%) on retail sales data signals institutional buying as recession fears recede. In a range-bound regime with slight bullish bias, buying into a beaten-down name that just broke above near-term resistance with volume is a solid momentum continuation setup. Defense spending tailwinds add secular support. Target $183.50 = 4.0% upside, stop $173.10 = 1.9% downside = 2.1:1 R:R.
recommendations.catalyst: Boeing surged 3.8% on Aug 15 on strong consumer/economic data easing recession fears. Industrials benefit from goldilocks macro—strong economy with rate cuts ahead. Momentum continuation play off a beaten-down name showing institutional accumulation.
